request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's crew total in `my-crew-due-total`, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx`; the server and stored data didn't need to change.

- **Whose crews:** it uses the same person as the existing "my due total", the one whose name or alias matches the user's name (trimmed, ignoring case). It shows blank when no one matches, or when that person leads no crew.
- **How it adds up:** it takes each crew that person leads and adds up its due-total, worked out the same way as `crew-due-total` on the crew rows (lead plus members, n/a totals skipped). A crew they're only a member of doesn't count.

The crew-total sum is now written out in both the header and the crews panel. Moving it into one shared helper would be a small tidy-up, but I left it as is.
